title: The Spring That Keeps All Its Versions

features.name: the spring's first voice
features.desc-on-touch: Where the water still speaks in the name it was given before anything else. The sound is clean and has not yet learned to change.

features.name: the keeping ground
features.desc-on-touch: Where all the versions of the spring rest beside each other, each with a different name, all from the same source.

features.name: the water's memory
features.desc-on-touch: This spring remembers being called river-mouth water, creek-source water, drought-refuge water, childhood-drink water. Each name is still true here.

features.name: the archive stone
features.desc-on-touch: A stone at the spring's edge, worn smooth by the touch of everyone who came to remember. Names are scratched into it, all the same water, all different.

features.name: the unbranching
features.desc-on-touch: Where the spring learns to hold more than one current at once, each version flowing back toward its own source moment.

inscription: the spring knows all its names at once and does not choose between them

file.name: Spring_Registry_All_Versions_Kept.mp3
file.note: A field recording made at three different seasons: each time the spring sounds different, yet each version is the same source speaking.

reverie.title: REVERIE — kneeling at the spring where all names meet
narr: you kneel at the spring's edge where she taught you
to listen: each name the water has ever held at once.
she doesn't speak. her hand rests in the cold flow.
the spring speaks in every voice it's ever borrowed.
"it's not keeping versions," she finally says. "it's
refusing to forget any way it has ever been loved."

exits.label: downriver, back toward the river's memory
upland toward the first source-spring's own source
toward the collecting pools where versions converge
